proposal: The Mandate recommends ending taxpayer funding of Planned Parenthood and other abortion providers: guidance that states may exclude them from Medicaid, a rule disqualifying elective-abortion providers from Medicaid, and congressional passage of a defunding bill. For Title X, it recommends rescinding the 2021 rule, reinstating the 2019 separation requirements, and expanding grantees beyond abortion providers.
remaining: A permanent statutory exclusion of abortion providers from Medicaid (the Mandate endorses the Protecting Life and Taxpayers Act); the one-year provision lapsed 2026-07-04 and no extension was found.
HHS guidance on state authority to exclude Planned Parenthood and a rule interpreting the Medicaid statute to disqualify elective-abortion providers (none found).

A Title X rule rescinding the 2021 regulation and reinstating the 2019 separation requirements (none proposed as of the sources reviewed; a senator asked HHS in April 2026 about its rulemaking timeline).
Expanding the Title X grantee pool beyond abortion providers (the April 2026 notices change grant priorities, but award outcomes were not found).
Decisions on the Section 1115 waiver requests from Idaho, South Carolina and Tennessee (no decision found).

status_summary: Section 71113 of Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) barred federal Medicaid payments to defined 'prohibited entities' (tax-exempt essential community providers mainly engaged in family planning that provide abortions outside narrow exceptions and received more than $800,000 in Medicaid payments in fiscal year 2023, including affiliates) for services in the one-year period starting on enactment, a definition the D. Mass. court found reaches Planned Parenthood Federation members and their affiliates (it counted 46 covered providers, 44 of them Federation members or possible affiliates). In Planned Parenthood Federation of America v. Kennedy (D. Mass. No. 1:25-cv-11913, Judge Talwani) the court granted preliminary injunctions against enforcing section 71113 against Federation members on 2025-07-21 and 2025-07-28 on First Amendment, equal protection and bill of attainder grounds and denied a stay on 2025-08-29, and then the First Circuit stayed those injunctions on 2025-09-11, vacated them in a judgment entered 2025-12-12, and on 2025-12-30 stayed a separate district court injunction obtained by states (No. 25-2165); the Federation plaintiffs then filed a notice of voluntary dismissal without prejudice of their D. Mass. suit on 2026-01-30. By its own terms the one-year period ended on 2026-07-04, and press reports say clinics resumed Medicaid billing for non-abortion services with no extension enacted before Congress recessed; extension efforts in 2026 (a Senate amendment in late April that failed, and calls for a third reconciliation bill) had not succeeded as of late July. On Title X, Sen. Josh Hawley's letter of 2026-04-02 says HHS released another year of funding under Title X grants approved under the prior administration, including to abortion providers such as Planned Parenthood, and that to his knowledge no rulemaking to reinstate the 2019 rule had begun. In addition, HHS's Office of Population Affairs lists a Fiscal Year 2027 Title X Services funding opportunity (PA-FPH-001, applications due 2027-01-11, up to $257 million for up to 90 awards, project periods up to five years) alongside research, infertility training and national training center opportunities; the Washington Examiner reports the April 2026 guidance and notices emphasize fertility-related conditions over contraception and restate that funds may not support programs where abortion is a method of family planning. The National Family Planning and Reproductive Health Association and a Pennsylvania grantee sued over the April changes in mid-June 2026, and Planned Parenthood Federation of America sued in the District of Columbia on 2026-07-28; no ruling was reported in either case. No rule reinstating the 2019 Title X regulation, no CMS guidance or rule on excluding abortion providers from Medicaid, and no action on the Idaho, South Carolina or Tennessee waiver requests were found.

timeline.event: Administration withholds Title X funds from all nine Planned Parenthood grantees (about $20.6 million) beginning late March to April 2025 (exact day not given, first of month used); some other grantees with Planned Parenthood clinics in their networks also receive withholding notices.

Public Law 119-21 is signed; section 71113 bars federal Medicaid payments to 'prohibited entities' for services furnished during the one-year period beginning on enactment (as described in the D. Mass. memorandum of 2025-07-28), defining such an entity as a 501(c)(3) essential community provider primarily engaged in family planning and related care that provides abortions outside narrow exceptions and received more than $800,000 in Medicaid payments in fiscal year 2023, including affiliates. Press reports attribute the one-year limit to Senate reconciliation rules.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts (via govinfo)

timeline.event: Judge Talwani (D. Mass. No. 1:25-cv-11913, Planned Parenthood Federation of America v. Kennedy) grants in part a preliminary injunction blocking enforcement of section 71113 against Federation members that will not provide abortions as of 2025-10-01 or whose fiscal year 2023 Medicaid payments did not exceed $800,000; on 2025-07-28 the court extends the injunction to all Federation members, finding plaintiffs likely to succeed on First Amendment, equal protection and bill of attainder claims. On 2025-08-29 the court denies the government's motion to stay the injunctions pending its First Circuit appeal.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts (via govinfo)

timeline.event: The First Circuit grants the government's stay pending appeal of the two D. Mass. preliminary injunctions (Nos. 25-1698 and 25-1755), as recounted in its order of 2025-09-18 denying reconsideration; section 71113 can therefore be applied to the Federation members.
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit (via Georgetown litigation tracker)

timeline.event: The First Circuit enters judgment in Nos. 25-1698 and 25-1755 vacating the district court's orders of 2025-07-21 and 2025-07-28 granting preliminary injunctions and remanding for further proceedings.
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit (via Georgetown litigation tracker)

timeline.event: In a separate suit by states against HHS (No. 25-2165), the First Circuit grants the government's motion for a stay pending appeal of a district court injunction that had barred section 71113 in its entirety, vacating its own administrative stay of 2025-12-08, and relying on its 2025-12-12 decision.
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit (via Georgetown litigation tracker)

timeline.event: Planned Parenthood Federation of America and two affiliates file a notice of voluntary dismissal without prejudice of all claims in D. Mass. No. 1:25-cv-11913 under Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i), ending that suit.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts, Document 106 (via Georgetown litigation tracker)

timeline.event: HHS issues Title X guidance and a notice of funding opportunity for 2027 services that emphasizes fertility-related chronic conditions and restates the statutory bar on funds for programs where abortion is a method of family planning; the same day Sen. Josh Hawley's office publicizes an April 2 letter objecting to HHS releasing another year of funding on Title X grants approved under the prior administration and asking about a timeline for rulemaking to reinstate the 2019 Title X rule.

The one-year Medicaid prohibition expires; reports on 2026-07-04 and 2026-07-22 say the provision lapsed, clinics resumed Medicaid billing for non-abortion services, and no extension had passed, though anti-abortion groups urged including one in a third reconciliation bill.

Planned Parenthood Federation of America sues HHS officials in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia (No. 1:26-cv-02656) over the April 2026 Title X funding notices as modified in July, alleging violations of the Administrative Procedure Act and the Spending Clause. No ruling reported.
